result.summary: RECONSTRUCTED HANDOFF -- written 2026-09-03 after the fact from the run's real, on-disk evidence: the current lib/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher.ex carries inline comments explicitly attributing config_from_snapshot/1's error-returning shape and do_attempt_dispatch/2's {:error, _malformed_reason} clause to 'BLOCKER fix (SECURITY-REVIEWER, queue task 415)' -- direct textual, on-disk confirmation that this finding was real and was made by SECURITY-REVIEWER at this step. Timestamps are reconstructed approximations. 1 BLOCKER, INV-8 (fail-loud/no-silent-catch discipline extended to this finding's actual failure mode -- an unhandled raise reaching a shared process). config_from_snapshot/1, as ELIXIR-DEV's initial pass wrote it, could raise (FunctionClauseError or ArgumentError-shaped) on a malformed config_snapshot -- a route_kind or method value outside its known set had no catch-all clause and would fall through every case/with clause without a match. Repo.transaction/1 does not swallow a raise (it propagates), so a single corrupted row (a future bug elsewhere writing a bad snapshot, a manual DB edit, or a value written before a later atom-set change) would crash the shared Poller GenServer mid-tick -- taking down every tenant's pending service_task_dispatches rows in that poll cycle, not merely failing the one bad row. This is a real availability hazard scoped beyond the single tenant that owns the malformed row: the Poller is a single shared process polling across all tenant schemas (confirmed by reading poller.ex's fetch_tenant_schemas/0 and its Enum.each over every provisioned schema), so one bad row degrades dispatch for the whole platform until the supervisor restarts it (and, per OTP restart-intensity limits, repeated crashes on the same poll cycle risk exceeding the supervisor's restart intensity entirely, per the identical hazard class Letflow.Scheduler.Poller's own boot-gating comment already documents for a different trigger). No SSRF/confidentiality/cross-tenant-reach issue was found -- INV-9's own placement (http_transport/3 calling UrlValidator.validate/2 immediately before do_http_transport/3, unconditionally, for the one shared transport call site both route_kind values that reach real HTTP funnel through) is structurally correct as written. This is filed as a correctness/availability BLOCKER under this project's INV-8 (no unhandled raise on a path that processes externally-influenced/stored data reaching a shared process), not a confidentiality or injection finding.

issues.description: config_from_snapshot/1 can raise (FunctionClauseError/ArgumentError-shaped) on a malformed config_snapshot (bad route_kind or method value) -- no catch-all clause exists. Repo.transaction/1 does not swallow a raise, so this crashes the shared Poller GenServer, taking down dispatch for every tenant's pending rows in that poll cycle. Fix: give route_kind_atom/1 and method_from_snapshot/1 explicit catch-all clauses returning a typed {:error, ...}; have config_from_snapshot/1 return {:ok, Config.t()} | {:error, :invalid_route_kind | :invalid_method}; wrap attempt_dispatch/2's outer call in a try/rescue mirroring Letflow.Scheduler.attempt_fire/2's exact shape (lib/letflow/scheduler.ex, its own try/rescue around fire_timer/2, converting any exception to {:error, {:raised, exception}}).
